finding.title: Batch OutboxProcessor's post-commit deleteRow/markAttempted cleanup instead of awaiting it per row

evidence.quote:
for (final id in ids) {
            await _dao.markAttempted(id, error: failedError.toString());

finding.why: pushCompletionsBatch exists specifically 'to eliminate the N-round-trip problem' by pushing up to _completionDrainCeiling=100000 rows in ≤500-op Firestore batches, but the local cleanup after that push still runs one awaited Drift statement per outbox row. For the large backlogs this ceiling anticipates (bulk_prior_completion_service / bulk_mark_screen can enqueue hundreds of completions at once, or a long offline stretch), this reintroduces the exact per-row round-trip cost DB-3 exists to prevent — now against the local DB — and materially lengthens the drain, which (per the concurrency finding above) increases the odds of tripping the drainStaleAfter race.
finding.recommendation: Add a bulk DAO method (e.g. deleteRows(List<int> ids) / markAttemptedBulk(List<int> ids, {required String error})) backed by a single batch()/DELETE...WHERE id IN(...) statement and call it once per commit/failure group instead of per row.
acceptance_criteria: New bulk DAO method(s) wrapped in a single transaction()/batch(); OutboxProcessor calls it once per outcome group.
Existing K3/K4 BatchPushException accounting tests continue to pass; add a test asserting the bulk DAO method is invoked exactly once for a multi-row commit/failure group.

evidence.quote: /// Tests for OutboxProcessor — covers drain() dispatch logic with a fake

finding.why: AG-3's own enforcement command (`find lib test -name '*.dart' ... | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'`) explicitly scans test/ too. outbox_processor.dart is 599 lines (50% over) and already a grab-bag of guard/backoff/dispatch/dead-letter/tutored/identity concerns; outbox_processor_test.dart is 1773 lines (4.4x over) but has 11 clean group() fault lines (single-flight, backoff, dead-letter, tutored-profile guard, identity-mismatch guard, offline behaviour, batch-size ceiling, FIFO ordering, BatchPushException accounting, revive-dead-letters, entity-kind constants) ready to split along.
finding.recommendation: Extract the backoff/dead-letter bookkeeping and the single-flight guard out of OutboxProcessor into small collaborators; split the test file along its existing group() boundaries into mirrored test/core/sync/outbox/outbox_processor_*_test.dart files.

finding.title: Add an AnalyticsEvent.outboxDeadLettered constant instead of reusing LogEvents.sync.outboxDeadLettered for analytics

evidence.quote: // All [AppLogger] call sites MUST use a constant from this file (or from a

finding.why: PV-5 requires every Analytics event to route through an AnalyticsEvent constant so one regex/format check and one searchable catalog cover all analytics traffic. LogEvents is documented (log_events.dart:6) as the AppLogger structured-log catalog, not the analytics one, and AnalyticsEvent (analytics_service.dart) does not list sync_outbox_dead_lettered at all — this analytics event is invisible to anyone auditing 'every analytics event we send' via AnalyticsEvent, and once custom_lint's no_raw_logevent check is un-broken it needs to catch this cross-catalog case, not just raw string literals.
finding.recommendation: Add `static const outboxDeadLettered = 'sync_outbox_dead_lettered';` to AnalyticsEvent and reference that at both call sites instead of LogEvents.sync.outboxDeadLettered.
acceptance_criteria: The PV-5 audit grep (or no_raw_logevent once custom_lint is fixed) confirms every logEvent( call site in this file references AnalyticsEvent.*.

finding.title: Replace outbox_processor.dart's raw 'sync_outbox_push_failed' literal with a LogEvents catalog constant
finding.why: log_events.dart's own header says every AppLogger call site MUST use a constant from that file rather than an ad-hoc string literal, but both AppLogger.instance.warning(...) calls here hand-type 'sync_outbox_push_failed' — a name distinct from the catalog's existing sync_push_failed. Two divergent event names now exist for 'a sync push failed'; anyone querying structured logs by the catalog constant misses these two sites, and renaming pushFailed's value later won't touch them.
finding.recommendation: Either reuse LogEvents.sync.pushFailed (if semantically equivalent) or add `String get outboxPushFailed => 'sync_outbox_push_failed';` to _SyncEvents and reference it from both call sites.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -n "event: '" lib/core/sync/outbox/outbox_processor.dart` returns no bare string-literal event names.

finding.title: Remove or justify PushPipeline.pushCompletion — OutboxProcessor never calls it
finding.why: OutboxProcessor's _dispatch switch has no case for OutboxEntityKind.completion — completions are handled exclusively via pushCompletionsBatch, consistent with the class doc's own warning ('Never call [pushCompletion] in a loop — that defeats the batching'). A repo-wide grep for `.pushCompletion(` shows the only caller of PushPipeline's (non-gateway) pushCompletion is test code calling it directly; production code never reaches it through the drain path. It's a fully implemented, individually tested, but currently unreachable interface method — dead surface area that invites drift (e.g. a future fix applied to pushCompletionsBatch but not mirrored here, or a future caller reintroducing the exact N-round-trip problem batching was built to eliminate).
finding.recommendation: Either delete pushCompletion from PushPipeline (and its implementation/tests) or add a doc comment on the interface method naming its actual sanctioned caller/purpose so the next reader doesn't mistake it for reachable code.
acceptance_criteria: Grep confirms either the method is removed (and OutboxPushPipeline/tests updated) or a doc comment states its real caller.
